LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard source URLs that point to GitHub releases for the termdock project, using versioned release assets. The `source` array entries fetch prebuilt binary tarballs for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures from the project's official GitHub repository, which is consistent with the declared upstream. The checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the build process.

During the execution of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the only executable portions are the top-level variable assignments and the implicit sourcing of the PKGBUILD. There is no command substitution, no execution of external scripts, and no network requests outside of the declared sources. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. All variables are statically defined or derived from safe string operations.

No code is executed during sourcing beyond simple bash expansions. The `package()` function is irrelevant for this gate, as it is not run under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD and downloading the sources poses no risk of remote code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Safe sourcing and source fetching</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD is for the `termdock-bin` package, a terminal multiplexer distributed as a precompiled binary. The source URLs point to GitHub releases under the legitimate author's repository (`https://github.com/padovanl/termdock`), and separate archives are provided for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The SHA-256 checksums are explicitly listed and match standard practice for verifying integrity of prebuilt binaries.

The package installs the binary to `/usr/bin`, places a sample config file in `/usr/share`, and installs documentation and license files in standard locations. All operations are confined to the package directory and follow standard Arch Linux packaging conventions. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, or execution of code during installation beyond extracting and placing verified files.

No obfuscated code, suspicious commands (like `curl|bash`), or unauthorized file manipulations are present. The use of `!strip` is appropriate for a binary package and does not indicate malicious intent. The package provides correct metadata, including license, conflicts, and provides fields. Everything aligns with safe, conventional AUR packaging for a prebuilt binary.
</details>
